newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Seagate, Gateway fall.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Seagate, Gateway fall.

text.p: Shares in computer industry companies Seagate Technology Inc and Gateway 2000 Inc fell in pre-open trade Wednesday, weighed down by warnings from the companies that quarterly results will fall short of expectations, traders said.
Seagate was at 36-1/2, down from a Tuesday close on the New York Stock Exchange of 41-1/2. Gateway 2000 fell to 30-3/8 from a closing price of 34-3/4.
"The two big things are Seagate and Gateway," a trader said. "They both reported they were going to miss their numbers."

Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers, said after the market closed Tuesday that it expected revenues for the second quarter to be about even with the first quarter's level of $1.42 billion.

Seagate, a maker of computer disk drives, issued its second earnings forecast in two weeks. It told investors after the market closed that revenues for the quarter ending June 27 were expected to be between $2 billion and $2.1 billion.
Both companies blamed the results on lackluster demand.

Oracle Corp ORCL.O also eased, trading at 50-1/4 from a closing Nasdaq price of 52-13/16. The software company reported fourth quarter earnings per share of $0.54, up from $0.40 for the same period a year before.
The earnings were in largely line with Wall Street expectations. However, one trader said, "You know these (technology) companies. If they don't blow out the numbers they get hit."
